To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the two-phase mass Sherwood number is a strong function of the solution inlet mass fraction and absorption pressure.

the overall heat and mass transfers in a vertical bubble absorption system are enhanced by decreasing the solution inlet temperature and mass fraction, increasing absorption pressure, decreasing orifice diameter and increasing solution inlet volumetric flow rate and vapor flow rate.

the overall heat and mass and two-phase mass-transfer coefficients increase with an increase in the Reynolds number, and decrease with an increase in orifice diameter, but the overall heat transfer coefficient decreases and the overall mass transfer coefficient increases with an increase in solution temperature and mass fractions.

the development of a reliable experimental apparatus and the experimental investigation on heat and transfer characteristics of a R124-NMP absorption pair in a vertical bubble glass absorber.
the heat and mass transfer of R124-NM P pair in a vertical bubble glass tube.
the experimental investigation of heat and mass transfer for R124-N-MP bubble absorption process in vertical glass bubble absorbers.

the experimental results can serve as a reference for the design and performance evaluation of absorption system.

a higher absorption pressure, solution flow rate, or solution inlet mass fraction, a smaller orifice diameter, and a larger solution inlet temperature and mass fraction can improve heat and mass transfer performance of a bubble absorber.

the experimental results can be well predicted by our proposed dimensionless correlations.

the overall and two-phase mass and heat transfer coefficients in a vertical bubble glass tube are strongly affected by the solution inlet temperature, inlet mass fraction and absorption pressure, and the two-phase mass and overall heat and mass transfers increase with an increase of the solution inlet mass fraction.

the dimensionless overall heat transfer coefficient, Sherwood number, and two-phase Sherwook number are the functions of dimensionless parameters of Rev, Res, orifice diameter, absorption pressure, and solution inlet mass fraction and temperature.
